div.div:
⟵ DELETED: hand-rolled ring + producer mainloop clock (airplay_source.rs).
RC2 (re-prebuffer) & RC3 (drift) solved NATIVELY, not patched — PipeWire's
adaptive resampler tracks the source clock with a DLL. A network jitter buffer
still exists, but PipeWire manages it on the graph clock.

div.div:
⟵ DELETED: overlay_mixer.rs + the in-relay per-device mix.
Duck = a volume node; announcement = a source linked into the node;
mix = the sink summing its inputs. Per-device volume becomes node Props
(exactly like RAOP today). This is O-B / O-E in
architecture-limitations-and-options.md.

⟵ The relay collapses to a thin, graph-paced egress:
capture → stamp → send. Nothing to preempt but the socket write.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1138px; height: 1px; padding-top: 781px; margin-left: 1262px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — validated on hardware (spike-results-and-status.md): ✓ per-device senders on a shared timeline (S1/S2) ✓ per-device volume (sendspin_volume.rs) ✓ per-device duck / announcement overlay (overlay_mixer.rs — in Rust) ✓ one per-device PipeWire node end-to-end (S3).
So the DEFAULT music path ALREADY splits a per-device sender per device — but fed from ONE steady anchor monitor, with the mix/duck still done in Rust. What this PROPOSED panel adds is only: (a) graph-native mixing (delete overlay_mixer), and (b) ingest adaptive rate-match.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1138px; height: 1px; padding-top: 953px; margin-left: 1262px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
⚠ HARDWARE FINDING that constrains this offload (S3): a STANDALONE per-device null-sink is NOT a steady clock driver — it produced ~1 audio glitch / 60 s (QUANT 0), while the one-anchor-monitor path showed zero downstream xruns. The team's conclusion was the OPPOSITE of naive per-device nodes: "feed a sync group from ONE anchor monitor, split only the sender."
⇒ Graph-native per-device mixing must use a STEADY-DRIVER node (e.g. a per-device volume / loopback chain hung off the steady anchor), NOT an independent null-sink per device. Also: per-device/anchor links must be PERSISTED & reconciled (a source-node rename silenced the anchor in the spike).

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 768px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1151px; margin-left: 32px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
MOVES INTO THE GRAPH (RT thread, graph clock — inherently jitter-free vs the app runtime):
• source-clock reconciliation + resampling → PipeWire adaptive resampler / RATE_MATCH
• routing → native links
• per-device volume + ducking → volume node / node Props
• announcement overlay + mixing → summing at the device sink

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 728px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1151px; margin-left: 832px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
DELETED FROM THE RUST PROCESS:
• the hand-rolled ingest ring + separate producer mainloop clock (airplay_source.rs)
• overlay_mixer.rs
• the per-device mix inside the sendspin relay
Less hand-rolled audio DSP + fewer app-runtime clocks = fewer places jitter can enter.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 808px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1151px; margin-left: 1592px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
STAYS IN RUST (irreducible — not graph operations):
• ALAC / AAC decode on ingest (codec)
• sendspin shared-timeline STAMPING + WebSocket transport
• AP2 RTP / ALAC / PTP egress
PipeWire has no WebSocket/sendspin clock domain, so the protocol egress can't live
in the graph. (A native WS sink module = O-C, considered & rejected: maintenance cost.)
Multi-room sync still needs the Rust timeline stamp — the graph doesn't carry it.

div.div: TRADE-OFFS: + each per-device node is RT-paced & jitter-free (vs one shared anchor differentiated in Rust); + per-device duck/announce/route without touching groupmates (fixes L1/L2/L5 in the arch doc). − more graph nodes ⇒ more graph CPU on the Pi (one sink + volume node per device); − a per-device capture per device instead of one anchor capture; − O-B needs a real node-per-sendspin-device (the strategic mechanism target — not yet built). Sequencing: land it AFTER the M1/M4 RT fixes are measured on hardware.
